subject: I can't compute standard errors in running lavaan (cross lagged effect model)

messages.author: 4a0d6ff9ce3b1d6b
messages.subject: I can't compute standard errors in running lavaan (cross lagged effect model)
parts:
Dear lavaan community, and have a nice to meet you,
I'm trying to  analyze cross-lagged effect model with lavaan in Rstudio.

The following is my code:
model2009 <-'
 #factor analysis(latent variables)
 ## I fix coefficient one in equation
  internal1 =~1*INFLU1+COMPLEX1
  institution1 =~ 1*PARTY1+ELECTION1+CONGRESS1
  internal2 =~1*INFLU2+COMPLEX2
  institution2 =~ 1*PARTY2+ELECTION2+CONGRESS2

 #unique variances of observed variables
  INFLU1~~INFLU1; COMPLEX1~~COMPLEX1; PARTY1~~PARTY1;           ELECTION1~~ELECTION1; CONGRESS1~~CONGRESS1
  INFLU2~~INFLU2; COMPLEX2~~COMPLEX2; PARTY2~~PARTY2;     ELECTION2~~ELECTION2; CONGRESS2~~CONGRESS2

 #structural equation
  internal2~internal1+institution1;
  institution2~internal1+institution1;

 #covariances between latent variables
  internal1~~institution1; internal2~~institution2; internal1~~internal1;     institution1~~institution1; internal2~~internal2; institution2~~institution2v
'

But I have a problem with computing standard errors as following messages:
警告メッセージ: 
1:  lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  で: 
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.
2:  lav_test_satorra_bentler(lavobject = NULL, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  で: 
  lavaan WARNING: could not invert information matrix needed for robust test statistic

3:  lavaan(model2009, panel.2009, ordered = c("PARTY1", "ELECTION1",  で: 
  lavaan WARNING: estimation of the baseline model failed.
4:  lav_object_post_check(object) で: 
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated lv variances are negative

I think the first warning is the main problem in not computing the standard errors. 

Actually I'm beginner of both Rstudio and lavaan, so this may be the elementary problem. 
Any insight is appreciated!

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: I can't compute standard errors in running lavaan (cross lagged effect model)
parts:
Ashu,

This is probably the key part to start on:

"
This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified."

internal2 is almost certainly not identified, with only two indicators and no outgoing structural paths. Depending on the strength of the structural paths, internal1 may also not be identified.

Broadly speaking, a latent variable needs at least three outgoing paths to be identified, whether to indicators or other latents, without additional constraints. internal2 does not meet this criterion. Though in this case you might be able to impose longitudinal measurement invariance for those "additional constraints." That will probably improve interpretability as well.

Try:

internal1 =~1*INFLU1+a*COMPLEX1
  institution1 =~ 1*PARTY1+b*ELECTION1+c*CONGRESS1
  internal2 =~1*INFLU2+a*COMPLEX2
  institution2 =~ 1*PARTY2+b*ELECTION2+c*CONGRESS2
